Example:

```tsx
import { ArchiveIcon, StarIcon, TrashIcon } from '@/components/ui/icons';
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/avatar';
import { SwipeActions } from '@/components/ui/swipe-actions';
import { toast } from '@/components/ui/toast';

const mails = [
  { name: 'Diya Rao', subject: 'Offer letter for Kabir', preview: 'Sent it this morning, joining is 3 Nov.' },
  { name: 'Finance', subject: 'September payroll is ready', preview: 'Please review and approve before Friday.' },
  { name: 'Rohan Das', subject: 'Laptop request', preview: 'Need a 16 GB machine for the new hire.' },
];

export default function SwipeActionsDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-2">
      {mails.map((m) => (
        <SwipeActions
          key={m.subject}
          actions={[
            { label: 'Star', icon: <StarIcon />, tone: 'warning', onClick: () => toast.info('Starred', m.subject) },
            { label: 'Archive', icon: <ArchiveIcon />, tone: 'primary', onClick: () => toast.success('Archived', m.subject) },
            { label: 'Delete', icon: <TrashIcon />, tone: 'danger', onClick: () => toast.error('Deleted', m.subject) },
          ]}
        >
          <div className="flex items-center gap-3 p-3">
            <Avatar name={m.name} />
            <div className="min-w-0"><p className="truncate text-[13px] font-medium">{m.subject}</p><p className="truncate text-xs text-muted-foreground">{m.name} · {m.preview}</p></div>
          </div>
        </SwipeActions>
      ))}
      <p className="px-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground">Swipe or drag a row left. Keyboard: focus a row, press Left.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Table (`table`)
Dense table parts with hover rows, a selected state, footer and caption.
- Group: Display
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add table`
- Import: `import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableFooter, TableCaption } from '@/components/ui/table'`

Example:

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/avatar';
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge';
import { Card } from '@/components/ui/card';
import { Progress } from '@/components/ui/progress';
import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableFooter, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from '@/components/ui/table';

const rows = [
  { id: 'INV-204', client: 'Northwind Traders', owner: 'Aarav Mehta', due: '12 Oct', paid: 100, amount: 4200, status: 'Paid' },
  { id: 'INV-205', client: 'Globex Corp', owner: 'Diya Rao', due: '18 Oct', paid: 40, amount: 1150, status: 'Due' },
  { id: 'INV-206', client: 'Initech', owner: 'Rohan Das', due: '02 Oct', paid: 0, amount: 8900, status: 'Overdue' },
  { id: 'INV-207', client: 'Umbrella Labs', owner: 'Isha Nair', due: '24 Oct', paid: 100, amount: 3275, status: 'Paid' },
  { id: 'INV-208', client: 'Stark Industries', owner: 'Kabir Shah', due: '28 Oct', paid: 65, amount: 12400, status: 'Due' },
  { id: 'INV-209', client: 'Wayne Enterprises', owner: 'Meera Iyer', due: '29 Sep', paid: 0, amount: 6050, status: 'Overdue' },
  { id: 'INV-210', client: 'Hooli', owner: 'Vikram Joshi', due: '05 Nov', paid: 100, amount: 2380, status: 'Paid' },
  { id: 'INV-211', client: 'Soylent Co', owner: 'Aarav Mehta', due: '09 Nov', paid: 15, amount: 5120, status: 'Due' },
];
const tone = { Paid: 'success', Due: 'warning', Overdue: 'danger' } as const;
const usd = (n: number) => `$${n.toLocaleString('en-US')}`;
const total = rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r.amount, 0);
const outstanding = rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r.amount * (1 - r.paid / 100), 0);

export default function TableDemo() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-full max-w-3xl overflow-hidden">
      <Table>
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow className="hover:bg-transparent">
            <TableHead>Invoice</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Client</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Owner</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Due</TableHead>
            <TableHead className="w-32">Collected</TableHead>
            <TableHead className="text-right">Amount</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Status</TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {rows.map((r) => (
            <TableRow key={r.id}>
              <TableCell className="whitespace-nowrap font-mono text-xs">{r.id}</TableCell>
              <TableCell className="whitespace-nowrap font-medium">{r.client}</TableCell>
              <TableCell><span className="flex items-center gap-2 whitespace-nowrap text-muted-foreground"><Avatar name={r.owner} size="sm" />{r.owner}</span></TableCell>
              <TableCell className="whitespace-nowrap text-muted-foreground">{r.due}</TableCell>
              <TableCell><Progress value={r.paid} aria-label={`${r.client} paid`} className="h-1.5" /></TableCell>
              <TableCell className="text-right tabular-nums">{usd(r.amount)}</TableCell>
              <TableCell><Badge variant={tone[r.status as keyof typeof tone]} dot>{r.status}</Badge></TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableBody>
        <TableFooter>
          <TableRow className="hover:bg-transparent">
            <TableCell colSpan={5}>Total · {usd(Math.round(outstanding))} outstanding</TableCell>
            <TableCell className="text-right tabular-nums">{usd(total)}</TableCell>
            <TableCell />
          </TableRow>
        </TableFooter>
        <TableCaption>October billing run, {rows.length} invoices</TableCaption>
      </Table>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## AI chat (`ai-chat`)
A whole AI chat in one piece: a conversation that follows the newest message with a Latest button, a greeting and starter prompts while empty, a thinking row and the prompt box pinned below.
- Group: AI
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add ai-chat`
- Import: `import { AiChat } from '@/components/ui/ai-chat'`
- Also needs: ai-message, icons, prompt-input, prompt-suggestions, thinking

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { AiChat, type AiChatMessage } from '@/components/ui/ai-chat';
import { CalendarIcon, FileTextIcon, UsersIcon } from '@/components/ui/icons';
import type { Suggestion } from '@/components/ui/prompt-suggestions';
import { StreamingText } from '@/components/ui/streaming-text';

const suggestions: Suggestion[] = [
  { id: '1', label: 'Summarise this week', hint: 'Attendance, leave and approvals', icon: <CalendarIcon /> },
  { id: '2', label: 'Draft an offer letter', hint: 'From a role and a salary', icon: <FileTextIcon /> },
  { id: '3', label: 'Who is out tomorrow?', hint: 'Across all teams', icon: <UsersIcon /> },
];

const replies = [
  'Here is the short version: 142 people are in, 9 are on leave, and 6 approvals are waiting for you. Attendance is up 2% on last week.',
  'Sure. I would start with the role, the band and the joining date, then add the notice period and the probation terms. Want me to draft it?',
];

export default function AiChatDemo() {
  const [messages, setMessages] = React.useState<AiChatMessage[]>([]);
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState('');
  const [thinking, setThinking] = React.useState(false);
  const [streaming, setStreaming] = React.useState(false);
  const n = React.useRef(0);
  const timers = React.useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>[]>([]);
  const send = (text: string) => {
    const reply = replies[n.current++ % replies.length]!;
    setValue('');
    setMessages((l) => [...l, { id: `u${Date.now()}`, role: 'user', content: text }]);
    setThinking(true);
    timers.current.push(setTimeout(() => {
      setThinking(false);
      setStreaming(true);
      setMessages((l) => [...l, { id: `a${Date.now()}`, role: 'assistant', plain: reply, streaming: true, content: <StreamingText text={reply} speed={20} caret={false} onDone={() => { setStreaming(false); setMessages((m) => m.map((x) => ({ ...x, streaming: false }))); }} /> }]);
    }, 1400));
  };
  const stop = () => { timers.current.forEach(clearTimeout); setThinking(false); setStreaming(false); setMessages((m) => m.map((x) => ({ ...x, streaming: false }))); };
  return (
    <AiChat
      className="max-w-2xl"
      messages={messages}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      onSubmit={send}
      onStop={stop}
      thinking={thinking}
      streaming={streaming || thinking}
      greeting="What are you working on?"
      suggestions={suggestions}
      onSuggestion={(s) => send(s.label)}
      placeholder="Message the assistant"
    />
  );
}
```

## AI message (`ai-message`)
One message in an AI chat: a right-aligned user bubble, or an assistant answer with copy, regenerate and thumbs actions and a blinking caret while it streams.
- Group: AI
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add ai-message`
- Import: `import { AiMessage } from '@/components/ui/ai-message'`
- Also needs: icons

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { AiMessage } from '@/components/ui/ai-message';
import { Cite } from '@/components/ui/sources';

export default function AiMessageDemo() {
  const [fb, setFb] = React.useState<'up' | 'down' | null>(null);
  const answer = 'Carry-forward is capped at 12 days a year, and anything above that lapses on 31 March.';
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-6">
      <AiMessage role="user">How many leave days can I carry forward?</AiMessage>
      <AiMessage role="assistant" plain={answer} onRegenerate={() => {}} feedback={fb} onFeedback={setFb}>
        <p>Carry-forward is capped at <strong>12 days</strong> a year<Cite n={1} href="#policy" title="Leave policy 2025" />, and anything above that lapses on 31 March<Cite n={2} href="#faq" title="Leave FAQ" />.</p>
        <p>Casual leave does not carry forward at all.</p>
      </AiMessage>
      <AiMessage role="assistant" streaming>Checking the policy for the part about encashment</AiMessage>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Attachment (`attachment`)
A file attached to a prompt: icon or thumbnail, name, size, an upload progress line, an error state and a remove button.
- Group: AI
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add attachment`
- Import: `import { Attachment } from '@/components/ui/attachment'`
- Also needs: icons

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Attachment } from '@/components/ui/attachment';

export default function AttachmentDemo() {
  const [files, setFiles] = React.useState(['offer-letter-v3.pdf', 'org-chart.png']);
  const [pct, setPct] = React.useState(35);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    const id = setInterval(() => setPct((p) => (p >= 100 ? 8 : p + 9)), 700);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, []);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      {files.map((f) => <Attachment key={f} name={f} size={f.endsWith('pdf') ? '248 KB' : '1.2 MB'} onRemove={() => setFiles((l) => l.filter((x) => x !== f))} />)}
      <Attachment name="payroll-october.xlsx" status="uploading" progress={pct} />
      <Attachment name="scan-0042.png" status="error" onRemove={() => {}} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Prompt input (`prompt-input`)
The box you type a prompt into: grows with the text, Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, and the send button turns into Stop while a reply streams.
- Group: AI
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add prompt-input`
- Import: `import { PromptInput } from '@/components/ui/prompt-input'`
- Also needs: icons

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { PaperclipIcon } from '@/components/ui/icons';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { PromptInput } from '@/components/ui/prompt-input';

export default function PromptInputDemo() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState('');
  const [streaming, setStreaming] = React.useState(false);
  const timer = React.useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(undefined);
  const send = () => {
    setValue('');
    setStreaming(true);
    timer.current = setTimeout(() => setStreaming(false), 3000);
  };
  const stop = () => { clearTimeout(timer.current); setStreaming(false); };
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-3">
      <PromptInput
        value={value}
        onValueChange={setValue}
        onSubmit={send}
        onStop={stop}
        streaming={streaming}
        maxLength={400}
        placeholder="Ask about leave policy, payroll or onboarding"
        leading={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Attach a file"><PaperclipIcon /></Button>}
      />
      <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line. After sending it shows Stop for three seconds.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Prompt suggestions (`prompt-suggestions`)
Starter prompts for an empty chat, as two-line cards or compact chips. Selecting one fills the prompt box.

```tsx
  { id: '3', label: 'Who is out tomorrow?', hint: 'Across all teams', icon: <UsersIcon /> },
  { id: '4', label: 'Explain this payslip', hint: 'Line by line, in plain words', icon: <SparkleIcon /> },

      <PromptSuggestions items={items} onSelect={(s) => setPicked(s.label)} />

  );
}
```

## Streaming text (`streaming-text`)
Text that arrives word by word, each word fading up out of a soft blur, with a caret that follows the last one. Screen readers get the full text at once.
- Group: AI
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add streaming-text`
- Import: `import { StreamingText } from '@/components/ui/streaming-text'`

Example:

```tsx

export default function StreamingTextDemo() {

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-4">
      <p className="min-h-24 text-sm leading-7"><StreamingText key={run} text={answer} speed={16} /></p>
```

```tsx
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Area chart (`area-chart`)
Smooth gradient areas, stacked or overlapping, that wipe in on scroll. Hover for a readout across series.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A line chart with the space under it filled in, so the total amount feels like volume. Stacked, it also shows what each part adds.
- How to read it: Stacked: the top edge is the total, each colored band is one part, and a band getting thicker means that part grew. Overlap mode compares series that each start at zero.
- Use it for: Traffic by source, revenue by plan, any total made of parts that changes over time.
- Skip it when: Many series (more than four bands get unreadable), or when you must compare the exact size of a middle band: its baseline moves, so use lines.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add area-chart`
- Import: `import { smoothPath, AreaChart } from '@/components/ui/area-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { AreaChart } from '@/components/ui/area-chart';
import { Segmented } from '@/components/ui/segmented';

export default function AreaChartDemo() {
  const [mode, setMode] = React.useState<'stacked' | 'overlap'>('stacked');
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-4">
      <Segmented value={mode} onValueChange={setMode} options={[{ value: 'stacked', label: 'Stacked' }, { value: 'overlap', label: 'Overlap' }]} className="justify-self-start" />
      <AreaChart
        stacked={mode === 'stacked'}
        labels={['Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct']}
        format={(n) => `${n}K`}
        series={[
          { name: 'Organic', data: [12, 14, 13, 18, 21, 24, 27] },
          { name: 'Paid', data: [6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 11, 14] },
          { name: 'Referral', data: [3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9] },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Bar list (`bar-list`)

## Bar race (`bar-race`)
Bars that re-sort and grow as time moves, frame by frame, with play and a scrubber. Shows who overtakes whom.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Horizontal bars ranked by value that re-sort and grow from one moment to the next.
- How to read it: The top bar is the leader at that moment. Press play to watch who overtakes whom, or drag the scrubber to a date to stop on it.
- Use it for: Rankings that change over time: cities, brands, teams, repositories.
- Skip it when: Anything that must be read precisely, or only two moments (use a slope chart).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add bar-race`
- Import: `import { BarRace } from '@/components/ui/bar-race'`

Example:

```tsx
import { BarRace } from '@/components/ui/bar-race';

const series: Record<string, number[]> = {
  Pune: [210, 260, 320, 410, 520, 640], Mumbai: [480, 510, 540, 560, 590, 610], Delhi: [390, 430, 480, 540, 600, 690],
  Bengaluru: [300, 380, 470, 590, 720, 880], Chennai: [250, 280, 310, 350, 400, 450], Hyderabad: [180, 240, 330, 430, 560, 700],
};
const years = ['2021', '2022', '2023', '2024', '2025', '2026'];

export default function BarRaceDemo() {
  return <BarRace className="w-[36rem] max-w-full" top={5} format={(n) => `${n}K`} frames={years.map((label, i) => ({ label, values: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(series).map(([k, v]) => [k, v[i]!])) }))} />;
}
```

## Box plot chart (`box-plot-chart`)
Spread per group: box for the middle half, median line, whiskers and outlier dots. Boxes open from the median; hover for the five numbers.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: The spread of values in each group, in five numbers: lowest, lower quarter, median, upper quarter, highest.
- How to read it: The line in the box is the median (the typical value). The box covers the middle half of the data. The whiskers reach the lowest and highest normal values. Dots are outliers. A tall box means the values vary a lot.
- Use it for: Response time per endpoint, salary per level, delivery days per carrier.
- Skip it when: Audiences who do not know statistics (add a short caption), or very small groups of fewer than 5 values.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add box-plot-chart`
- Import: `import { BoxPlotChart } from '@/components/ui/box-plot-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { BoxPlotChart } from '@/components/ui/box-plot-chart';

export default function BoxPlotChartDemo() {
  return (
    <BoxPlotChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      format={(n) => `${n}ms`}
      groups={[
        { label: '/login', min: 40, q1: 70, median: 95, q3: 130, max: 190, outliers: [260, 310] },
        { label: '/search', min: 90, q1: 140, median: 210, q3: 320, max: 480, outliers: [620] },
        { label: '/orders', min: 60, q1: 110, median: 150, q3: 190, max: 260 },
        { label: '/export', min: 300, q1: 520, median: 740, q3: 980, max: 1400, outliers: [1750] },
        { label: '/health', min: 8, q1: 12, median: 15, q3: 19, max: 28 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Bullet chart (`bullet-chart`)
A KPI against its target in one thin row, with shaded bands for poor, ok and good. The bar slides in on scroll.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One measure against its target, in a single thin row. It replaces a gauge and uses less space.
- How to read it: The dark or colored bar is the actual value. The vertical tick is the target. The shaded bands behind are poor, okay and good ranges. A bar that passes the tick beat the target.
- Use it for: KPIs vs goals: revenue vs quota, uptime vs SLA, NPS vs target.
- Skip it when: A single number with no target or range: use a stat card.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add bullet-chart`
- Import: `import { BulletChart } from '@/components/ui/bullet-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { BulletChart } from '@/components/ui/bullet-chart';

export default function BulletChartDemo() {
  return (
    <BulletChart
      className="w-[34rem] max-w-full"
      rows={[
        { label: 'Revenue (₹L)', value: 72, target: 66, ranges: [40, 60, 90] },
        { label: 'New customers', value: 118, target: 150, ranges: [80, 120, 180] },
        { label: 'Uptime (%)', value: 99.94, target: 99.9, ranges: [99, 99.5, 100] },
        { label: 'NPS', value: 41, target: 50, ranges: [20, 40, 70] },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Bump chart (`bump-chart`)
Rank over time as smooth lines that swap places. Lines draw in one by one; hover a line or name to follow it.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How rank changes over time. Not the values, only the order.
- How to read it: Each line is one item. Numbers in the dots are ranks, with 1 at the top. A line moving up means the item climbed. Crossing lines swapped places.
- Use it for: Leaderboards by month, search position, product popularity, league tables.
- Skip it when: When the gap between ranks matters (first can be far ahead of second): use a line chart of the values.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add bump-chart`
- Import: `import { BumpChart } from '@/components/ui/bump-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { BumpChart } from '@/components/ui/bump-chart';

export default function BumpChartDemo() {
  return (
    <BumpChart
      className="w-[38rem] max-w-full"
      labels={['Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct']}
      series={[
        { name: 'Pune', ranks: [1, 1, 2, 3, 2] },
        { name: 'Mumbai', ranks: [2, 3, 1, 1, 1] },
        { name: 'Delhi', ranks: [3, 2, 3, 2, 3] },
        { name: 'Bengaluru', ranks: [4, 4, 4, 4, 4] },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Butterfly chart (`butterfly-chart`)
Two bar sets back to back around shared rows, like a population pyramid. Bars grow outward from the middle.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Two sets of bars back to back around a shared list. Also called a population pyramid.
- How to read it: The center column names each row. Bars to the left belong to the left group, bars to the right to the right group. Longer is more. Compare the two sides row by row.
- Use it for: Population by age and gender, desktop vs mobile per page, hires and exits per team.
- Skip it when: Groups that are not comparable, or a single group. Use a bar chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add butterfly-chart`
- Import: `import { ButterflyChart } from '@/components/ui/butterfly-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { ButterflyChart } from '@/components/ui/butterfly-chart';

export default function ButterflyChartDemo() {
  return (
    <ButterflyChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      leftLabel="Mobile"
      rightLabel="Desktop"
      rows={[
        { label: 'Home', left: 5200, right: 3100 }, { label: 'Pricing', left: 3400, right: 4200 }, { label: 'Docs', left: 1800, right: 5600 },
        { label: 'Blog', left: 4100, right: 2300 }, { label: 'Signup', left: 2600, right: 2900 }, { label: 'Settings', left: 700, right: 1900 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Candlestick chart (`candlestick-chart`)
Open, high, low and close per period. Green closed up, red closed down. Candles grow from their midpoint in sequence; hover for the four numbers.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Open, high, low and close for each period, used for prices.
- How to read it: The thick body runs from the open to the close. Green means the close was higher than the open, red means lower. The thin line (the wick) reaches the highest and lowest value in the period.
- Use it for: Share prices, currency rates, any value with a daily range.
- Skip it when: Data with only one value per period: use a line chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add candlestick-chart`
- Import: `import { CandlestickChart } from '@/components/ui/candlestick-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { CandlestickChart, type Candle } from '@/components/ui/candlestick-chart';

// Deterministic walk so the demo looks the same every time.
const rnd = (i: number) => { const x = Math.sin(i * 12.9898) * 43758.5453; return x - Math.floor(x); };
const data: Candle[] = (() => {
  let price = 100;
  return Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => {
    const open = price;
    const close = open + (rnd(i) - 0.45) * 8;
    price = close;
    return { label: `D${i + 1}`, open, close, high: Math.max(open, close) + rnd(i + 50) * 3, low: Math.min(open, close) - rnd(i + 90) * 3 };
  });
})();

export default function CandlestickChartDemo() {
  return <CandlestickChart className="w-full max-w-xl" data={data} />;
}
```

## Charts (`charts`)
Sparkline, bar chart and donut in plain SVG. No chart library.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Three small charts: a sparkline (a tiny trend line), a bar chart, and a donut (share of a whole).
- How to read it: Sparkline: only the shape matters, left is older, right is newer. Bars: taller means more. Donut: a bigger slice means a bigger share, and the slices add up to 100%.
- Use it for: Sparkline inside a stat card, bars to compare a few categories, donut for a split like plan mix.
- Skip it when: Donut with more than five or six slices, or when you need exact numbers: use a table or bar list instead.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add charts`
- Import: `import { useChartIn, Sparkline, BarChart, DonutChart } from '@/components/ui/charts'`

Example:

```tsx
import { BarChart, DonutChart, Sparkline } from '@/components/ui/charts';
import { Card } from '@/components/ui/card';

export default function ChartsDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full gap-4 lg:grid-cols-2">
      <Card className="p-5">
        <p className="mb-4 text-sm font-semibold">Leads per month</p>
        <BarChart data={[{ label: 'May', value: 38 }, { label: 'Jun', value: 52 }, { label: 'Jul', value: 47 }, { label: 'Aug', value: 66 }, { label: 'Sep', value: 59 }, { label: 'Oct', value: 81 }]} />
      </Card>
      <Card className="grid gap-5 p-5">
        <p className="text-sm font-semibold">Lead source</p>
        <DonutChart
          centerLabel={<div><p className="text-xl font-semibold leading-none">342</p><p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">leads</p></div>}
          data={[{ label: 'Website', value: 140 }, { label: 'Referral', value: 90 }, { label: 'Events', value: 70 }, { label: 'Cold outreach', value: 42 }]}
        />
        <div className="h-10 w-40"><Sparkline data={[4, 6, 5, 8, 7, 10, 9, 13]} /></div>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Chord chart (`chord-chart`)
Flow between every pair of items around a circle. Arcs sweep in, then ribbons fade in; hover an item to keep only its ribbons.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How much flows between every pair of items, drawn around a circle.
- How to read it: Each arc on the ring is one item. A ribbon joining two arcs is the flow between them. A wider ribbon is more flow. Hover an item to keep only its ribbons.
- Use it for: Migration between cities, messages between teams, trades between desks.
- Skip it when: More than about 10 items (it turns into a tangle), or when direction matters a lot. A sankey shows direction better.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add chord-chart`
- Import: `import { ChordChart } from '@/components/ui/chord-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { ChordChart } from '@/components/ui/chord-chart';

export default function ChordChartDemo() {
  return (
    <ChordChart
      size={340}
      labels={['Pune', 'Mumbai', 'Delhi', 'Bengaluru', 'Chennai']}
      matrix={[
        [0, 120, 40, 60, 20],
        [110, 0, 70, 50, 30],
        [30, 80, 0, 90, 25],
        [70, 40, 100, 0, 85],
        [15, 35, 20, 95, 0],
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Circle pack chart (`circle-pack-chart`)
One bubble per item, area by value, packed into a cluster. Bubbles pop out from the center biggest first; hover for the share.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Bubbles packed together, one per item, where the area of each bubble is its value.
- How to read it: A bigger bubble is a bigger value. Biggest sits in the middle. Compare areas, not widths. Hover a bubble for its exact share.
- Use it for: Users by country, revenue by customer, tags by use: lots of items with a few giants and a long tail.
- Skip it when: Close values (people misjudge circle area) and anything that needs an order. A lollipop or bar chart ranks better.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add circle-pack-chart`
- Import: `import { CirclePackChart } from '@/components/ui/circle-pack-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx

        { label: 'Germany', value: 800 }, { label: 'Singapore', value: 700 }, { label: 'Canada', value: 520 }, { label: 'Brazil', value: 380 },
        { label: 'Japan', value: 300 }, { label: 'Kenya', value: 160 }, { label: 'Chile', value: 90 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Cohort table (`cohort-table`)
Retention triangle: a row per signup group, a column per period, each cell the percent still active and tinted by it.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A triangle of percentages: one row per group of users by when they joined, one column per period since.
- How to read it: Each cell is the percent of that group still active after that many periods; darker is better. Read across a row to see one group decay, down a column to see whether newer groups retain better than older ones. Hover a cell for the head count.
- Use it for: Subscription and product retention by signup month, repeat purchases, class attendance.
- Skip it when: Fewer than four groups, or data with no clear start date per user.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add cohort-table`
- Import: `import { CohortTable } from '@/components/ui/cohort-table'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { CohortTable } from '@/components/ui/cohort-table';

export default function CohortTableDemo() {
  return (
    <CohortTable
      className="w-[40rem] max-w-full"
      cohorts={[
        { label: 'May 2026', size: 1240, retention: [100, 62, 48, 41, 37, 34] },
        { label: 'Jun 2026', size: 1410, retention: [100, 66, 51, 44, 40] },
        { label: 'Jul 2026', size: 1580, retention: [100, 64, 50, 43] },
        { label: 'Aug 2026', size: 1722, retention: [100, 69, 55] },
        { label: 'Sep 2026', size: 1895, retention: [100, 71] },
        { label: 'Oct 2026', size: 2010, retention: [100] },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Combo chart (`combo-chart`)
Bars, smooth lines and smooth areas on one chart, with an optional second scale on the right. Many values read together; hover a month for all of them.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Bars, smooth lines and smooth areas drawn together on one chart.
- How to read it: Bars show amounts per period, lines show a trend, a shaded area shows a target or range. A line marked with the right-hand scale uses that scale, not the left. Hover a period to read every value; hover a legend name to isolate one series.
- Use it for: Revenue bars with a conversion line, sales against a target, volume and rate over the same months.
- Skip it when: More than about 4 series or 12 periods, or a right-hand scale that confuses readers. Split into two charts.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add combo-chart`
- Import: `import { ComboChart } from '@/components/ui/combo-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import { ComboChart } from '@/components/ui/combo-chart';

/** Bars stacked (remove `stacked` for side by side) and smooth lines on one chart. The conversion line uses the right-hand scale. */
export default function ComboChartDemo() {
  return (
    <ComboChart
      className="w-[38rem] max-w-full"
      stacked
      labels={['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep']}
      format={(n) => `$${n}k`}
      formatRight={(n) => `${n}%`}
      series={[
        { name: 'Revenue', type: 'bar', data: [42, 48, 45, 58, 63, 60, 72, 78, 85] },
        { name: 'Costs', type: 'bar', data: [30, 33, 35, 38, 41, 44, 46, 49, 52], color: 'text-destructive' },
        { name: 'Target', type: 'area', data: [70, 78, 84, 92, 100, 106, 114, 122, 130], color: 'text-warning' },
        { name: 'Conversion', type: 'line', axis: 'right', data: [2.1, 2.4, 2.2, 2.9, 3.1, 3, 3.6, 3.9, 4.3], color: 'text-success' },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Data table (`data-table`)
Sortable columns, a search box and pagination, with optional row selection and bulk actions, column visibility menu, sticky header, toolbar slot, row action menus and clickable rows. You pass rows and column definitions.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add data-table`
- Import: `import { DataTable } from '@/components/ui/data-table'`
- Also needs: button, checkbox, dropdown-menu, icons, pagination, table

Example:

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/avatar';
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { DataTable, type Column } from '@/components/ui/data-table';
import { TooltipProvider, TruncatedText } from '@/components/ui/tooltip';

interface Person { id: string; name: string; email: string; team: string; city: string; joined: string; salary: number; status: 'Active' | 'On leave' | 'Notice' }

const people: Person[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Aarav Mehta', email: 'aarav.mehta@acme.in', team: 'Engineering', city: 'Pune', joined: '2021-03-15', salary: 1850000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '2', name: 'Diya Rao', email: 'diya.rao@acme.in', team: 'Design', city: 'Bengaluru', joined: '2022-07-01', salary: 1420000, status: 'On leave' },
  { id: '3', name: 'Rohan Das', email: 'rohan.das@acme.in', team: 'Sales', city: 'Mumbai', joined: '2023-01-09', salary: 960000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '4', name: 'Isha Nair', email: 'isha.nair@acme.in', team: 'People Ops', city: 'Kochi', joined: '2020-11-23', salary: 1100000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '5', name: 'Kabir Shah', email: 'kabir.shah@acme.in', team: 'Engineering', city: 'Ahmedabad', joined: '2019-05-06', salary: 2250000, status: 'Notice' },
  { id: '6', name: 'Meera Iyer', email: 'meera.iyer@acme.in', team: 'Finance', city: 'Chennai', joined: '2022-02-14', salary: 1380000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '7', name: 'Vikram Joshi', email: 'vikram.joshi@acme.in', team: 'Sales', city: 'Nashik', joined: '2023-08-21', salary: 880000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '8', name: 'Ananya Kulkarni', email: 'ananya.kulkarni@acme.in', team: 'Engineering', city: 'Pune', joined: '2024-01-08', salary: 1620000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '9', name: 'Siddharth Verma', email: 'siddharth.verma@acme.in', team: 'Support', city: 'Delhi', joined: '2021-09-30', salary: 720000, status: 'On leave' },
  { id: '10', name: 'Tara Menon', email: 'tara.menon@acme.in', team: 'Design', city: 'Bengaluru', joined: '2023-04-17', salary: 1290000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '11', name: 'Nikhil Patil', email: 'nikhil.patil@acme.in', team: 'Finance', city: 'Nagpur', joined: '2020-06-02', salary: 1540000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '12', name: 'Pooja Desai', email: 'pooja.desai@acme.in', team: 'People Ops', city: 'Surat', joined: '2024-05-13', salary: 940000, status: 'Notice' },
  { id: '13', name: 'Arjun Reddy', email: 'arjun.reddy@acme.in', team: 'Engineering', city: 'Hyderabad', joined: '2022-10-10', salary: 1980000, status: 'Active' },
  { id: '14', name: 'Kavya Bhat', email: 'kavya.bhat@acme.in', team: 'Support', city: 'Mysuru', joined: '2023-12-04', salary: 690000, status: 'Active' },
];

const tone = { Active: 'success', 'On leave': 'warning', Notice: 'danger' } as const;
const date = (d: string) => new Date(d).toLocaleDateString('en-IN', { day: '2-digit', month: 'short', year: 'numeric' });

const columns: Column<Person>[] = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true, value: (p) => p.name, render: (p) => <span className="flex items-center gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><Avatar name={p.name} size="sm" />{p.name}</span> },
  { key: 'email', header: 'Email', value: (p) => p.email, render: (p) => <TruncatedText className="w-36 text-muted-foreground">{p.email}</TruncatedText> },
  { key: 'team', header: 'Team', sortable: true, value: (p) => p.team },
  { key: 'joined', header: 'Joined', sortable: true, value: (p) => p.joined, render: (p) => <span className="whitespace-nowrap text-muted-foreground">{date(p.joined)}</span> },
  { key: 'salary', header: 'Salary', sortable: true, align: 'right', value: (p) => p.salary, render: (p) => `₹${(p.salary / 100000).toFixed(1)}L` },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', value: (p) => p.status, render: (p) => <Badge variant={tone[p.status]} dot>{p.status}</Badge> },
];

export default function DataTableDemo() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <DataTable
        className="w-full"
        rows={people}
        columns={columns}
        rowKey={(p) => p.id}
        pageSize={6}
        filterPlaceholder="Filter people"
        selectable
        columnMenu
        bulkActions={(rows, clear) => (
          <>
            <Button size="xs" variant="outline" onClick={clear}>Export {rows.length}</Button>
            <Button size="xs" variant="ghost" onClick={clear}>Clear</Button>
          </>
        )}
      />
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Dumbbell chart (`dumbbell-chart`)
Change per item as two dots joined by a line: before and after, plan and actual. Green when good, red when bad.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Change per item, shown as two dots joined by a line.
- How to read it: The hollow dot is the earlier value, the filled dot the later one. A longer line means a bigger change. Green means a good change, red a bad one.
- Use it for: Before and after, plan vs actual, this year vs last year across many items.
- Skip it when: More than two moments in time (use lines), or a single item.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add dumbbell-chart`
- Import: `import { DumbbellChart } from '@/components/ui/dumbbell-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

```tsx
      toLabel="2026"

        { label: 'Engineering', from: 62, to: 78 },
        { label: 'Sales', from: 71, to: 69 },
        { label: 'Support', from: 55, to: 74 },
        { label: 'Marketing', from: 68, to: 81 },
        { label: 'Finance', from: 80, to: 77 },
      ]}
```

## File manager (`file-manager`)
Folder browser with breadcrumb, list and grid views, selection and double-click or Enter to open.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add file-manager`
- Import: `import { FileManager } from '@/components/ui/file-manager'`
- Also needs: icons

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { FileManager, type FileItem } from '@/components/ui/file-manager';

const tree: Record<string, FileItem[]> = {
  '': [
    { id: 'hr', name: 'HR', type: 'folder', modified: '07 Oct' },
    { id: 'fin', name: 'Finance', type: 'folder', modified: '05 Oct' },
    { id: 'brand', name: 'Brand assets', type: 'folder', modified: '28 Sep' },
    { id: 'readme', name: 'Welcome.pdf', type: 'file', size: 482000, modified: '01 Sep' },
  ],
  hr: [
    { id: 'policy', name: 'Leave policy 2026.pdf', type: 'file', size: 910000, modified: '06 Oct' },
    { id: 'offer', name: 'Offer letter template.docx', type: 'file', size: 64000, modified: '02 Oct' },
    { id: 'org', name: 'Org chart.png', type: 'image', size: 1840000, modified: '30 Sep' },
  ],
  fin: [
    { id: 'p', name: 'Payroll September.xlsx', type: 'file', size: 233000, modified: '05 Oct' },
    { id: 'inv', name: 'Invoices', type: 'folder', modified: '03 Oct' },
  ],
  brand: [
    { id: 'logo', name: 'Logo.png', type: 'image', size: 54000, modified: '12 Sep' },
    { id: 'guide', name: 'Brand guide.pdf', type: 'file', size: 5200000, modified: '12 Sep' },
  ],
  inv: [{ id: 'i1', name: 'INV-204.pdf', type: 'file', size: 88000, modified: '03 Oct' }],
};

export default function FileManagerDemo() {
  const [trail, setTrail] = React.useState<{ id: string; name: string }[]>([]);
  const here = trail.length ? trail[trail.length - 1].id : '';
  return (
    <FileManager
      className="max-w-xl"
      path={['Files', ...trail.map((t) => t.name)]}
      items={tree[here] ?? []}
      onNavigate={(d) => setTrail(trail.slice(0, d))}
      onOpen={(it) => it.type === 'folder' && setTrail([...trail, { id: it.id, name: it.name }])}
    />
  );
}
```

## Forecast chart (`forecast-chart`)
Solid line for what happened, dashed line inside a shaded band for what is expected. The band is the likely range.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: What happened so far, plus what we expect next with a range around it.
- How to read it: The solid line is real data. After the vertical divider the dashed line is the prediction and the shaded band is the likely range. A wider band means less certainty.
- Use it for: Revenue, demand or headcount projections where you want to show uncertainty honestly.
- Skip it when: Predictions with no real uncertainty estimate: a band you made up is worse than a plain dashed line.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add forecast-chart`
- Import: `import { ForecastChart } from '@/components/ui/forecast-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import { ForecastChart } from '@/components/ui/forecast-chart';

export default function ForecastChartDemo() {
  return (
    <ForecastChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      format={(n) => `₹${n}L`}
      labels={['Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec', 'Jan', 'Feb']}
      actual={[42, 48, 45, 58, 63, 61, 72]}
      forecast={[76, 81, 84, 90]}
      low={[72, 74, 74, 77]}
      high={[80, 88, 94, 103]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Funnel chart (`funnel-chart`)
Conversion funnel with a bar per stage and the step-to-step rate.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How many people drop off at each step of a process.
- How to read it: Each bar is a step, widest first. The gap between two bars is the drop-off. The percentage is how many made it from the step before.
- Use it for: Signup flow, sales pipeline, checkout steps.
- Skip it when: Steps that are not in order, or processes where people can skip steps.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add funnel-chart`
- Import: `import { FunnelChart } from '@/components/ui/funnel-chart'`

Example:

```tsx
import { FunnelChart } from '@/components/ui/funnel-chart';

export default function FunnelChartDemo() {
  return <FunnelChart className="max-w-xl" dropoff stages={[{ label: 'Visitors', value: 48200 }, { label: 'Sign-ups', value: 9640 }, { label: 'Qualified', value: 3120 }, { label: 'Demo booked', value: 1210 }, { label: 'Won', value: 340 }]} />;
}
```

## Gantt chart (`gantt`)
Schedule view with a bar per task, progress fill, weekend shading and a today line.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Tasks as bars on a calendar, so you see when each starts, ends and overlaps.
- How to read it: Each row is a task. The bar runs from its start to its end date. The filled part is progress. The vertical line is today.
- Use it for: Project plans, roadmaps, team schedules.
- Skip it when: Tasks without dates, or very large plans (use a roadmap board).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add gantt`
- Import: `import { Gantt } from '@/components/ui/gantt'`

Example:

```tsx
import { Gantt, type GanttTask } from '@/components/ui/gantt';

const d = (offset: number) => { const t = new Date(); t.setDate(t.getDate() + offset); return `${t.getFullYear()}-${String(t.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(t.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`; };

const tasks: GanttTask[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Discovery', owner: 'Isha Nair', start: d(-10), end: d(-4), progress: 100, tone: 'success' },
  { id: '2', name: 'Design system', owner: 'Diya Rao', start: d(-6), end: d(3), progress: 70, tone: 'info' },
  { id: '3', name: 'Backend APIs', owner: 'Rohan Das', start: d(-3), end: d(9), progress: 40 },
  { id: '4', name: 'Frontend build', owner: 'Aarav Mehta', start: d(1), end: d(14), progress: 10 },
  { id: '5', name: 'QA and fixes', owner: 'Vikram Joshi', start: d(10), end: d(18), progress: 0, tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '6', name: 'Launch', owner: 'Meera Iyer', start: d(19), end: d(21), progress: 0, tone: 'danger' },
];

export default function GanttDemo() {
  return <Gantt tasks={tasks} />;
}
```

## Gauge (`gauge`)
Half-circle meter with a needle that swings to the value.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One number against a range, like a car speedometer.
- How to read it: The needle and filled arc show where the value sits between the minimum and maximum. Colored zones tell you if that is good, so a needle in green is fine.
- Use it for: A single health score, CPU load, quota used.
- Skip it when: More than one measure, or precise values. Pair with the number printed in the middle.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add gauge`
- Import: `import { Gauge } from '@/components/ui/gauge'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Gauge } from '@/components/ui/gauge';
import { Slider } from '@/components/ui/slider';

export default function GaugeDemo() {
  const [v, setV] = React.useState(72);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-4">
      <Gauge value={v} label="Team engagement" />
      <Slider aria-label="Gauge value" className="w-56" value={v} onValueChange={setV} showValue={false} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Half donut chart (`half-donut-chart`)
A semicircle split into parts with a total under the arch. Half the height of a donut, so it fits dashboard cards.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A semicircle split into parts, with a total or headline number under the arch.
- How to read it: The full arch is the whole (or the maximum if you set one). Each colored arc is one part. An empty stretch at the end is the unused part.
- Use it for: Budget used, storage by file type, seats by group, a dashboard card with little height.
- Skip it when: Many parts, or values that need precise comparison.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add half-donut-chart`
- Import: `import { HalfDonutChart } from '@/components/ui/half-donut-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

```tsx
export default function HalfDonutChartDemo() {

}
```

## Heat calendar (`heat-calendar`)
One month as a calendar grid, every day tinted by its value. Hover a day for its number; click to select.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One month as a calendar, each day tinted by its value.
- How to read it: Darker days have more, empty grey days have no data. Hover or focus a day to read its number; click a day to select it.
- Use it for: Daily sales, tickets, attendance or commits for a single month.
- Skip it when: More than one month at a time. Use the year heatmap.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add heat-calendar`
- Import: `import { HeatCalendar } from '@/components/ui/heat-calendar'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { HeatCalendar } from '@/components/ui/heat-calendar';

/** October 2026, one number per day (leave a day out for no data). */
export default function HeatCalendarDemo() {
  const values = Array.from({ length: 31 }, (_, i) => (i % 7 === 5 || i % 7 === 6 ? undefined : Math.round(20 + 60 * Math.abs(Math.sin(i * 1.7)))));
  return <HeatCalendar year={2026} month={10} values={values} format={(n) => `${n} deals`} />;
}
```

## Heatmap (`heatmap`)
Contribution-style grid for daily activity. Cells pop in column by column.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Activity per day over many weeks, like the GitHub contribution graph.
- How to read it: Each square is a day. Darker means more activity. Each column is a week and each row is a weekday, so streaks look like dark lines.
- Use it for: Check-ins, commits, support tickets per day, habit tracking.
- Skip it when: Short spans of a few days, or when exact counts matter (hover shows them, but a table is clearer).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add heatmap`
- Import: `import { Heatmap } from '@/components/ui/heatmap'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Heatmap } from '@/components/ui/heatmap';

export default function HeatmapDemo() {
  // Deterministic pseudo-random so the demo looks the same every time.
  const values = React.useMemo(() => Array.from({ length: 26 * 7 }, (_, i) => {
    const x = Math.sin(i * 12.9898) * 43758.5453;
    const r = x - Math.floor(x);
    const weekend = i % 7 === 0 || i % 7 === 6;
    return r < (weekend ? 0.6 : 0.2) ? 0 : Math.floor(r * 12);
  }), []);
  return <Heatmap values={values} unit="check-ins" />;
}
```

## Histogram chart (`histogram-chart`)
Counts how many values fall in each range from raw data, with a smooth curve over the bars. Bars rise in turn.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How many values fall into each range.
- How to read it: Each bar is a range of values. Taller means more values land there. The shape tells you the story: a hill in the middle is typical, a long tail means a few big values, two humps mean two groups.
- Use it for: Order sizes, response times, ages, exam scores.
- Skip it when: Categories (use a bar chart), or fewer than about 30 values.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add histogram-chart`
- Import: `import { HistogramChart } from '@/components/ui/histogram-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { HistogramChart } from '@/components/ui/histogram-chart';

// Deterministic pseudo-random bell-ish values so the demo looks the same every time.
const rnd = (i: number) => { const x = Math.sin(i * 12.9898) * 43758.5453; return x - Math.floor(x); };

export default function HistogramChartDemo() {
  const values = React.useMemo(() => Array.from({ length: 400 }, (_, i) => Math.round(2400 + (rnd(i) + rnd(i + 400) + rnd(i + 800) - 1.5) * 1900)), []);
  return <HistogramChart className="w-[36rem] max-w-full" values={values} bins={14} format={(n) => `₹${Math.round(n)}`} />;
}
```

## India map (`india-map`)
India by state and union territory, with a 3D bar or pin standing on every state in your data. Zoom and pan it; click a name in the list to highlight a state.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: India drawn state by state, with a bar or pin standing on each state you have data for.
- How to read it: A taller bar (or bigger pin) and a darker state mean a bigger number. Hover or click a state, or a row in the list, for its name and value.
- Use it for: Orders, customers or users by state, where the place matters more than the exact number.
- Skip it when: Comparing close values (use a bar list next to it), or anything finer than a state (districts, cities).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add india-map`
- Import: `import { indiaRegionNames, IndiaMap } from '@/components/ui/india-map'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { IndiaMap } from '@/components/ui/india-map';
import { Segmented } from '@/components/ui/segmented';

const data = [
  { id: 'M1', label: 'M1 (Maharashtra + Goa)', value: 19280 },
  { id: 'South', value: 34210 },
  { id: 'Delhi', value: 11380 },
  { id: 'Gujarat', value: 8240 },
  { id: 'Uttar Pradesh', value: 7610 },
  { id: 'West Bengal', value: 4120 },
  { id: 'Rajasthan', value: 3560 },
  { id: 'Punjab', value: 2480 },
  { id: 'Assam', value: 1390 },
];

// Merge states into your own regions: the region name is what you use as `id` in the data.
const groups = {
  M1: ['Maharashtra', 'Goa'],
  South: ['Karnataka', 'Tamil Nadu', 'Kerala', 'Telangana', 'Andhra Pradesh'],
};

export default function IndiaMapDemo() {
  const [marker, setMarker] = useState<'bar' | 'pin'>('bar');
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full gap-4">
      <Segmented value={marker} onValueChange={setMarker} options={[{ value: 'bar', label: 'Bars' }, { value: 'pin', label: 'Pins' }]} className="justify-self-start" />
      <IndiaMap data={data} groups={groups} marker={marker} format={(n) => `${n.toLocaleString('en-IN')} orders`} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Kanban board (`kanban`)
Columns of draggable cards. Drag with the mouse or move a focused card with Alt and the arrow keys. Controlled, no drag library.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add kanban`
- Import: `import { Kanban } from '@/components/ui/kanban'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/avatar';
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge';
import { Kanban, type KanbanColumn } from '@/components/ui/kanban';

interface Task { id: string; title: string; tag: string; owner: string; due: string }

const columns: KanbanColumn[] = [
  { id: 'todo', title: 'To do', tone: 'default' },
  { id: 'doing', title: 'In progress', tone: 'info' },
  { id: 'review', title: 'In review', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: 'done', title: 'Done', tone: 'success' },
];

const tagTone = { Bug: 'danger', Feature: 'info', Chore: 'default', Design: 'warning' } as const;

export default function KanbanDemo() {
  const [board, setBoard] = React.useState<Record<string, Task[]>>({
    todo: [
      { id: 't1', title: 'Onboarding checklist for new hires', tag: 'Feature', owner: 'Isha Nair', due: '14 Oct' },
      { id: 't2', title: 'Fix payslip PDF margins', tag: 'Bug', owner: 'Rohan Das', due: '12 Oct' },
      { id: 't3', title: 'Archive 2023 attendance logs', tag: 'Chore', owner: 'Meera Iyer', due: '30 Oct' },
    ],
    doing: [
      { id: 't4', title: 'Leave balance widget', tag: 'Feature', owner: 'Aarav Mehta', due: '16 Oct' },
      { id: 't5', title: 'Refresh login screen', tag: 'Design', owner: 'Diya Rao', due: '15 Oct' },
    ],
    review: [{ id: 't6', title: 'Holiday calendar import', tag: 'Feature', owner: 'Kabir Shah', due: '11 Oct' }],
    done: [
      { id: 't7', title: 'Dark mode for dashboards', tag: 'Design', owner: 'Diya Rao', due: '03 Oct' },
      { id: 't8', title: 'Duplicate employee IDs', tag: 'Bug', owner: 'Vikram Joshi', due: '05 Oct' },
    ],
  });
  return (
    <Kanban
      columns={columns}
      value={board}
      onChange={setBoard}
      renderCard={(t) => (
        <div className="grid gap-2">
          <p className="font-medium leading-snug">{t.title}</p>
          <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
            <Badge variant={tagTone[t.tag as keyof typeof tagTone]}>{t.tag}</Badge>
            <span className="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs text-muted-foreground">{t.due}<Avatar name={t.owner} size="xs" /></span>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    />
  );
}
```

## Line chart (`line-chart`)
Multi-series line or area chart in plain SVG with grid, axis labels, legend and a hover readout.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How one or more numbers change over time.
- How to read it: Left to right is time. Higher is more. A line going up is growth, down is decline. Hover to read exact values.
- Use it for: Revenue by month, signups by week, anything where the trend matters more than any single point.
- Skip it when: Comparing categories with no time order (use bars), or fewer than 4 points (a stat card says it better).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add line-chart`
- Import: `import { LineChart } from '@/components/ui/line-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

```tsx
        area

          { name: 'Revenue', data: [42, 48, 45, 58, 63, 61, 72] },
          { name: 'Payroll', data: [30, 31, 31, 34, 36, 36, 38], color: 'text-warning' },
          { name: 'Profit', data: [12, 17, 14, 24, 27, 25, 34], color: 'text-success' },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Live chart (`live-chart`)
Streaming line chart that slides left as new values arrive. You give it a function for the next value; pause it any time.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A line that keeps moving as fresh numbers arrive, like a heart-rate monitor.
- How to read it: The right edge is now; older values slide off to the left. The tag at the top right is the latest value.
- Use it for: Active users right now, requests per second, CPU, queue length.
- Skip it when: Historical analysis. It forgets old points; use a line or area chart for a full history.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add live-chart`
- Import: `import { LiveChart } from '@/components/ui/live-chart'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { LiveChart } from '@/components/ui/live-chart';

export default function LiveChartDemo() {
  const [paused, setPaused] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-3">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between"><span className="text-sm font-medium">Active users</span><Button size="xs" variant="outline" onClick={() => setPaused(!paused)}>{paused ? 'Resume' : 'Pause'}</Button></div>
      <LiveChart paused={paused} next={(p) => Math.max(10, Math.min(95, p + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 14))} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Lollipop chart (`lollipop-chart`)
A bar chart as a thin stick with a dot on the end, sorted largest first. Lighter than bars when there are many items.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A bar chart drawn with a thin stick and a dot. Same message, less ink.
- How to read it: The further the dot from the left, the bigger the value. Sorted biggest first so the ranking reads from the top.
- Use it for: Many items to rank: tickets per customer, bugs per module.
- Skip it when: Only two or three items: a plain bar is fine.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add lollipop-chart`
- Import: `import { LollipopChart } from '@/components/ui/lollipop-chart'`

```tsx
      ]}
    />
  );
```

## Marimekko chart (`marimekko-chart`)
Stacked 100% bars whose widths also mean something: column width is group size, block height is mix. Columns grow up on scroll.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Stacked 100% bars where the width of each column is also data. Also called a mosaic or Mekko chart.
- How to read it: Column width is how big that group is. Block height is the mix inside it. A block's area is its share of everything. Hover a block for both percentages.
- Use it for: Market share by region (wide regions are bigger markets), plan mix per customer segment.
- Skip it when: More than five blocks per column, or when widths do not carry meaning: use a stacked bar chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add marimekko-chart`
- Import: `import { MarimekkoChart } from '@/components/ui/marimekko-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { MarimekkoChart } from '@/components/ui/marimekko-chart';

export default function MarimekkoChartDemo() {
  return (
    <MarimekkoChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      format={(n) => `₹${n}L`}
      keys={[{ key: 'pro', label: 'Pro' }, { key: 'biz', label: 'Business', color: 'text-success' }, { key: 'starter', label: 'Starter', color: 'text-warning' }]}
      columns={[
        { label: 'North', values: { pro: 40, biz: 30, starter: 10 } },
        { label: 'West', values: { pro: 55, biz: 50, starter: 20 } },
        { label: 'South', values: { pro: 30, biz: 20, starter: 25 } },
        { label: 'East', values: { pro: 10, biz: 8, starter: 12 } },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Matrix heatmap (`matrix-heatmap`)
Rows by columns shaded by value: traffic by hour and weekday, cohort retention. Cells fade in as a wave; hover lights up the row and column.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A grid where the color of each cell shows a value: rows by columns.
- How to read it: Find a row and a column, read the cell where they meet. Darker or brighter means a bigger number. Look for bright clusters and dark gaps.
- Use it for: Traffic by hour and weekday, cohort retention by month, errors by service and day.
- Skip it when: When you need to compare exact values (colors are hard to compare closely), or hundreds of rows. Turn on showValues to print the numbers.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add matrix-heatmap`
- Import: `import { MatrixHeatmap } from '@/components/ui/matrix-heatmap'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { MatrixHeatmap } from '@/components/ui/matrix-heatmap';

const rows = ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun'];
const cols = ['6a', '8a', '10a', '12p', '2p', '4p', '6p', '8p', '10p'];
// Busy weekday mid-mornings and afternoons, quiet weekends.
const values = rows.map((_, r) => cols.map((_, c) => Math.round((r > 4 ? 6 : 20) * (1 + Math.sin((c + 1) * 0.9) * 0.8) + ((r * 7 + c * 13) % 9))));

export default function MatrixHeatmapDemo() {
  return <MatrixHeatmap className="w-full max-w-xl" rows={rows} cols={cols} values={values} showValues format={(n) => String(Math.max(0, n))} />;
}
```

## Network graph (`network-graph`)
Dots joined by lines for services, people or links. Settled layout (no jitter); hover lights up neighbours, click selects.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Dots for things and lines for the links between them.
- How to read it: A bigger dot has more links. Dots drawn close together are tightly connected. Hover a dot to light up what it touches.
- Use it for: Service dependencies, who talks to whom, related topics.
- Skip it when: More than about 60 nodes or dense links, which become a hairball. Use a chord or sankey chart instead.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add network-graph`
- Import: `import { NetworkGraph } from '@/components/ui/network-graph'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { NetworkGraph } from '@/components/ui/network-graph';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'api', label: 'API gateway', group: 0 }, { id: 'auth', label: 'Auth', group: 0 }, { id: 'users', label: 'Users', group: 1 }, { id: 'billing', label: 'Billing', group: 1 },
  { id: 'orders', label: 'Orders', group: 1 }, { id: 'search', label: 'Search', group: 1 }, { id: 'pg', label: 'Postgres', group: 2 }, { id: 'redis', label: 'Redis', group: 2 },
  { id: 'queue', label: 'Queue', group: 2 }, { id: 'mail', label: 'Mailer', group: 3 }, { id: 'pay', label: 'Payments', group: 3 },
];
const links = [
  ['api', 'auth'], ['api', 'users'], ['api', 'orders'], ['api', 'search'], ['api', 'billing'], ['auth', 'redis'], ['users', 'pg'], ['orders', 'pg'], ['orders', 'queue'],
  ['billing', 'pg'], ['billing', 'pay'], ['queue', 'mail'], ['search', 'redis'], ['orders', 'pay'],
].map(([source, target]) => ({ source: source!, target: target! }));

export default function NetworkGraphDemo() {
  return <NetworkGraph className="w-[42rem] max-w-full" nodes={nodes} links={links} groups={[{ name: 'Edge' }, { name: 'Services' }, { name: 'Stores' }, { name: 'External' }]} />;
}
```

## Outcome bar (`outcome-bar`)
One thick rounded bar split green and red in proportion (won vs lost), a pale piece for what is still open, a big conversion number above and the counts under each part.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One bar split into parts in proportion, such as won and lost, with a pale part for what is still open.
- How to read it: The big number is the first part (won) out of the counted parts (won plus lost); the open part is not counted. Wider means more. Each count sits under its own part.
- Use it for: Win rate, pass and fail, approved and rejected, with a count of what is still pending.
- Skip it when: More than about four parts, or values that are not parts of one whole. Use a bar or pie chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add outcome-bar`
- Import: `import { OutcomeBar } from '@/components/ui/outcome-bar'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { OutcomeBar } from '@/components/ui/outcome-bar';

/** 4 won, 17 lost, 51 still open: the headline is won out of closed (19%). */
export default function OutcomeBarDemo() {
  return (
    <OutcomeBar
      className="w-[26rem] max-w-full"
      headlineLabel="conversion"
      segments={[{ label: 'Won', value: 4 }, { label: 'Lost', value: 17 }]}
      ghost={{ label: 'Open', value: 51 }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Pace chart (`pace-chart`)
Burn-up for a monthly target: running total, the straight line you should be on, a dashed projection to month end, the target line and an ahead or behind pace chip.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A running total against a target for the month, with where you should be and where you are heading.
- How to read it: The solid line is the total so far. The faint straight line is the pace needed to hit the target by month end. The dashed line carries today's daily rate to month end; if it ends below the target line you are behind. The chip says by how much.
- Use it for: Monthly sales or revenue target, a budget burning down, any goal with a deadline.
- Skip it when: Data that is not cumulative, or targets with no end date.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add pace-chart`
- Import: `import { PaceChart } from '@/components/ui/pace-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { PaceChart } from '@/components/ui/pace-chart';

/** Cumulative won value to day 17 of a 30 day month, against a target of 42.8 Cr. */
export default function PaceChartDemo() {
  const daily = [0.4, 0.4, 1.1, 0.9, 1.6, 0.8, 2.4, 1.2, 0.7, 0.7, 1.6, 1.0, 1.3, 0.8, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2];
  let total = 0;
  const points = daily.map((v, i) => ({ day: i + 1, value: +(total += v).toFixed(2) }));
  return <PaceChart className="w-[34rem] max-w-full" points={points} target={42.8} daysInMonth={30} format={(n) => `₹${n.toFixed(2)} Cr`} />;
}
```

## Parallel coordinates (`parallel-coordinates`)
One vertical axis per measure and one line per item crossing each at its value. Compare many measures at once; hover to isolate a line.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One vertical axis for each measure, and one line per item that crosses every axis at its value.
- How to read it: Lines that run side by side are alike on those measures; lines that cross between two axes are opposites there. Hover a line to isolate it and read its exact values.
- Use it for: Comparing items on four to eight measures at once: products, cars, candidates, regions.
- Skip it when: Fewer than three measures (use a scatter) or more than about 30 lines (they turn to noise).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add parallel-coordinates`
- Import: `import { ParallelCoordinates } from '@/components/ui/parallel-coordinates'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { ParallelCoordinates } from '@/components/ui/parallel-coordinates';

const cars = [
  ['Sedan A', 28, 210, 6.1, 14.2, 0], ['Sedan B', 31, 190, 7.4, 13.1, 0], ['Hatch C', 38, 160, 9.8, 11.4, 0], ['Hatch D', 36, 170, 9.1, 11.9, 0],
  ['SUV E', 22, 230, 8.2, 21.5, 1], ['SUV F', 24, 215, 8.9, 19.8, 1], ['SUV G', 20, 250, 7.1, 26.0, 1],
  ['EV H', 0, 260, 4.6, 38.0, 2], ['EV I', 0, 220, 6.2, 31.5, 2], ['EV J', 0, 190, 7.8, 24.9, 2],
] as const;

export default function ParallelCoordinatesDemo() {
  return (
    <ParallelCoordinates
      className="w-[42rem] max-w-full"
      axes={[
        { key: 'mpg', label: 'Mileage', format: (n) => `${n} km/l` },
        { key: 'top', label: 'Top speed', format: (n) => `${n} km/h` },
        { key: 'acc', label: '0-100 s', format: (n) => `${n}s` },
        { key: 'price', label: 'Price', format: (n) => `₹${n}L` },
      ]}
      groups={[{ name: 'Petrol' }, { name: 'Diesel SUV' }, { name: 'Electric' }]}
      rows={cars.map(([name, mpg, top, acc, price, group]) => ({ name, group, values: { mpg, top, acc, price } }))}
    />
  );
}
```

## Pareto chart (`pareto-chart`)
Causes sorted by size as bars plus a running-total line with an 80% mark. Shows which few causes matter most.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Causes sorted biggest to smallest as bars, plus a running-total line.
- How to read it: Read the bars left to right: the biggest cause first. The line shows the running percent of the total. Where it crosses the dashed 80% line is how many causes make up most of the problem.
- Use it for: Finding the few causes behind most defects, tickets or costs (the 80/20 rule).
- Skip it when: Items that are not causes of one total, or fewer than five items.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add pareto-chart`
- Import: `import { ParetoChart } from '@/components/ui/pareto-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import { ParetoChart } from '@/components/ui/pareto-chart';

export default function ParetoChartDemo() {
  return (
    <ParetoChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      items={[
        { label: 'Login', value: 142 }, { label: 'Billing', value: 96 }, { label: 'Slow', value: 61 }, { label: 'Export', value: 28 },
        { label: 'Mobile', value: 17 }, { label: 'Search', value: 11 }, { label: 'Other', value: 9 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Permission matrix (`permission-matrix`)
Roles by permissions grid of checkboxes with per-column toggle and locked roles.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add permission-matrix`
- Import: `import { PermissionMatrix } from '@/components/ui/permission-matrix'`
- Also needs: checkbox, table

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { PermissionMatrix, type Grants } from '@/components/ui/permission-matrix';

const roles = [
  { id: 'owner', label: 'Owner', hint: 'Always full access' },
  { id: 'admin', label: 'Admin', hint: 'Manages people and settings' },
  { id: 'finance', label: 'Finance', hint: 'Invoices and payouts' },
  { id: 'manager', label: 'Manager', hint: 'Own team only' },
  { id: 'support', label: 'Support', hint: 'Customer tickets' },
  { id: 'viewer', label: 'Viewer', hint: 'Read-only' },
];
const permissions = [
  { id: 'view', label: 'View' },
  { id: 'create', label: 'Create' },
  { id: 'edit', label: 'Edit' },
  { id: 'delete', label: 'Delete' },
  { id: 'approve', label: 'Approve' },
  { id: 'export', label: 'Export' },
  { id: 'billing', label: 'Billing' },
];

export default function PermissionMatrixDemo() {
  const [grants, setGrants] = React.useState<Grants>({
    owner: ['view', 'create', 'edit', 'delete', 'approve', 'export', 'billing'],
    admin: ['view', 'create', 'edit', 'delete', 'approve', 'export'],
    finance: ['view', 'create', 'edit', 'approve', 'export', 'billing'],
    manager: ['view', 'create', 'edit', 'approve'],
    support: ['view', 'create', 'edit'],
    viewer: ['view'],
  });
  return <PermissionMatrix className="w-full max-w-3xl" roles={roles} permissions={permissions} value={grants} onChange={setGrants} locked={['owner']} />;
}
```

## Pie chart (`pie-chart`)
Slices of one whole that sweep around on scroll. Hover a slice or legend row and it pulls out.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One whole divided into slices.
- How to read it: A bigger slice is a bigger share. The slices add up to 100%. Hover a slice to pull it out and see the value.
- Use it for: Three to five parts of a whole: plan mix, traffic by source.
- Skip it when: Many slices, similar-sized slices (hard to tell apart), or comparing across several pies. Use a bar chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add pie-chart`
- Import: `import { PieChart } from '@/components/ui/pie-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx

      className="w-[32rem] max-w-full"
      format={(n) => `₹${n}L`}
      data={[{ label: 'Pro plan', value: 48 }, { label: 'Business', value: 31 }, { label: 'Starter', value: 14, color: 'text-warning' }, { label: 'Add-ons', value: 7, color: 'text-info' }]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Pivot table (`pivot-table`)
Cross-tab of your rows: one field down the side, another across the top, sum, count, average, min or max in each cell, with totals and heat shading.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add pivot-table`
- Import: `import { PivotTable } from '@/components/ui/pivot-table'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { PivotTable } from '@/components/ui/pivot-table';
import { Segmented } from '@/components/ui/segmented';

const regions = ['North', 'South', 'West', 'East'];
const quarters = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4'];
const products = ['Starter', 'Growth', 'Scale'];
const sales = regions.flatMap((region, i) => quarters.flatMap((quarter, j) => products.map((product, k) => ({ region, quarter, product, revenue: ((i + 2) * (j + 3) * (k + 1) * 37_000) % 900_000 + 120_000 }))));

export default function PivotTableDemo() {
  const [by, setBy] = React.useState<'quarter' | 'product'>('quarter');
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full gap-4">
      <Segmented value={by} onValueChange={setBy} options={[{ value: 'quarter', label: 'By quarter' }, { value: 'product', label: 'By product' }]} />
      <PivotTable data={sales} rows="region" columns={by} value="revenue" rowLabel="Region" format={(n) => `₹${(n / 100_000).toFixed(1)}L`} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Progress ring (`progress-ring`)
Circular progress with an eased stroke animation.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One percentage shown as a circle that fills up.
- How to read it: A full circle is 100%. The number in the middle is the exact value.
- Use it for: Profile completion, upload progress, a single KPI vs target.
- Skip it when: Several values at once: use radial-bar-chart or a progress bar list.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add progress-ring`
- Import: `import { ProgressRing } from '@/components/ui/progress-ring'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { ProgressRing } from '@/components/ui/progress-ring';

export default function ProgressRingDemo() {
  const [v, setV] = React.useState(0);
  React.useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => setV(72), 100); return () => clearTimeout(t); }, []);
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-8">
      <ProgressRing value={v} aria-label="Upload progress" />
      <ProgressRing value={v / 2} aria-label="Setup progress" size={72} stroke={6} className="text-success" />
      <button className="text-sm text-primary hover:underline" onClick={() => setV((x) => (x === 72 ? 30 : 72))}>Animate</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Punch card chart (`punch-card-chart`)
A grid of dots where dot size is the value, like commits by weekday and hour. Dots pop in on a diagonal wave.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A grid of dots where the size of a dot is the value.
- How to read it: Find a row and a column; a bigger dot where they meet is a bigger value. Look for rows or columns with big dots in a line.
- Use it for: Commits by weekday and hour, tickets by day and shift, orders by slot. Smaller grids than a heatmap.
- Skip it when: Large grids over about 10 by 24, where dots blur together. Use a matrix heatmap.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add punch-card-chart`
- Import: `import { PunchCardChart } from '@/components/ui/punch-card-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { PunchCardChart } from '@/components/ui/punch-card-chart';

const rows = ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun'];
const cols = ['6a', '8a', '10a', '12p', '2p', '4p', '6p', '8p', '10p'];
const values = rows.map((_, r) => cols.map((_, c) => Math.max(0, Math.round((r > 4 ? 4 : 18) * (1 + Math.sin((c + 1) * 0.9) * 0.9) + ((r * 5 + c * 11) % 7) - 3))));

export default function PunchCardChartDemo() {
  return <PunchCardChart className="w-[34rem] max-w-full" rows={rows} cols={cols} values={values} format={(n) => `${n} commits`} />;
}
```

## Radar chart (`radar-chart`)
Spider chart for several scores on the same axes: a pentagon with five, a hexagon with six. Shapes grow from the center on scroll; hover a legend name to highlight a series.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Several scores for one thing on the same scale, drawn as a polygon. With five axes it is a pentagon, with six a hexagon. Also called a spider or web chart.
- How to read it: Each spoke is one skill or measure; the further the corner from the center, the higher the score. A big, even shape is well rounded; a lopsided shape has a weak spot. Compare shapes, not exact numbers.
- Use it for: Skill profiles, team reviews, product vs competitor on 5 to 8 qualities, player stats.
- Skip it when: Axes that are not on the same scale, more than 8 axes, or more than 3 shapes at once. Use bars when exact comparison matters.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add radar-chart`
- Import: `import { RadarChart } from '@/components/ui/radar-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { RadarChart } from '@/components/ui/radar-chart';

/** Five axes make a pentagon; add or remove an axis and the shape follows. */
export default function RadarChartDemo() {
  return (
    <RadarChart
      axes={['Delivery', 'Quality', 'Communication', 'Ownership', 'Teamwork']}
      series={[
        { name: 'Aarav', values: [88, 82, 70, 90, 76] },
        { name: 'Team average', values: [72, 74, 78, 68, 80] },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Radial bar chart (`radial-bar-chart`)
Concentric rings, one per goal, that sweep in on scroll. Legend hover highlights a ring; the middle takes any content.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Several progress rings nested inside each other, one ring per goal.
- How to read it: A ring is full at the target (100%). A longer arc means closer to the goal. Outer rings are longer, so compare the percentages, not the arc length.
- Use it for: Goals vs target on a dashboard: calls, revenue, tickets closed. Fitness-style activity rings.
- Skip it when: Comparing raw values across rings, or more than five rings.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add radial-bar-chart`
- Import: `import { RadialBarChart } from '@/components/ui/radial-bar-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx

export default function RadialBarChartDemo() {
  return (
    <RadialBarChart
      className="w-full max-w-sm"
      data={[{ label: 'Revenue', value: 82 }, { label: 'New leads', value: 64 }, { label: 'Tickets closed', value: 91 }, { label: 'NPS', value: 48 }]}
    >
      <div className="grid"><span className="text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums">71%</span><span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">of target</span></div>
    </RadialBarChart>
  );
}
```

## Radial line chart (`radial-line-chart`)
A line chart bent into a circle for things that repeat: 24 hours, 12 months. A smooth closed shape grows from the middle.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A line chart bent into a circle so the end meets the start. Good for things that repeat.
- How to read it: Each spoke is one label, like an hour or a month. Distance from the center is the value. A bulge shows a busy period. Move over the chart to read the nearest spoke.
- Use it for: 24 hours, 12 months or 7 weekdays: traffic by hour, sales by month.
- Skip it when: Data that does not repeat (the start and end join, which is misleading), or exact comparison. Use a line chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add radial-line-chart`
- Import: `import { RadialLineChart } from '@/components/ui/radial-line-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { RadialLineChart } from '@/components/ui/radial-line-chart';

export default function RadialLineChartDemo() {
  const hours = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, h) => `${h}`);
  const day = (peak: number, width: number, height: number) => hours.map((_, h) => { const d = Math.min(Math.abs(h - peak), 24 - Math.abs(h - peak)); return Math.round(6 + height * Math.exp(-(d * d) / (2 * width * width))); });
  return <RadialLineChart labels={hours} format={(n) => `${n} req/s`} series={[{ name: 'Web', data: day(14, 3.2, 90) }, { name: 'Mobile', data: day(21, 2.4, 70), color: 'text-success' }]} />;
}
```

## Range gauge (`range-gauge`)
Speedometer in coloured bands (poor, fair, good) with a needle that swings to the value and a big number.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A speedometer split into coloured bands with a needle on the current value.
- How to read it: The needle points at the value on the scale. The band it sits in (and the word under the number) tells you if that is poor, fair, good or excellent.
- Use it for: Scores with known zones: credit score, health score, NPS, uptime.
- Skip it when: Values with no meaningful zones. Use the plain gauge or a progress ring.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add range-gauge`

